name: html-selector-list-percentage-height-chain
description: A flex row with a definite height stretches its items, and each item's `height:100%` wrappers carry that height down to a `position:absolute` `object-fit:cover` image. The wrappers get their `height:100%` from one rule scoped by a data attribute on the item, whose target is an `:is()` selector list: `.item[data-kind="media"] :is(.item-body,.item-frame)`. The converted item drops the data attribute, so the rule must be projected onto marker classes like any other attribute-scoped rule. The selector matcher read an `:is()`/`:where()` argument only as one compound, so a list made the whole selector unsupported: the rule stayed verbatim and matched nothing, the wrappers lost their height, the `.frame-box` `height:100%` below them was demoted to `height:auto` for want of a sized ancestor, and the cover image collapsed to 1px.

source_reference.notes: Regression coverage for Automattic/blocks-engine#2170: absolutely positioned fill images collapsed to 1px under wrappers sized by an attribute-scoped `:is()` rule.

legacy_comparison.reason: This upstream primitive fixture has no downstream legacy comparison.
